Riti & ParamparaV12

A 40 × 20 ft section in two halves. Riti, on the east, walks the sixteen samskaras along a lit timeline that wraps the walls. Parampara, on the west, shows six traditions that turn everyday acts into devotion and ends at the Char Dham wall: four glowing pieces of India, each threaded to its dham. Drag to orbit, scroll or pinch to zoom, right-drag or Shift-drag to pan, double-click a spot to zoom in, and click any piece. Walk around puts you at eye level, moving with WASD, the arrow keys or the on-screen pad. Teal labels are the Riti additions and orange “P idea” labels are the Parampara additions: switch each one on or off in the bars above the model.

Three statement pieces

The three things people will remember. Everything else in each half supports them.

Riti · sixteen milestones

The glowing samskara timeline

A dark strip runs about 42 ft round the Riti walls with the six section names cut through it and lit from behind. Above it, sixteen cards each show one samskara: artwork, its name, how to say it, and what it means.

Build2 in fire-rated foam or PVC strip, 9½ in tall, on 2½ in standoffs so it stands 4½ in off the wall at 3′–3′10″, with the chapter boards right above it at 4′–6′8″. White diffusion behind the letters, warm LED tape inside and along both edges. Cards 18 × 27 in, one clamp spot each.

Parampara · light becomes knowledge

The Arti alcove

A dark recess on the south wall lit only by rows of diyas, the way arti began. Visitors step into the warm light and place a diya on the steps. The back wall is either a TV playing an arti video or the poster: switch between them with the Arti alcove buttons above the model.

BuildTwo 4 ft plywood returns, a 1 ft valance and a black scrim canopy, painted near-black inside. Three diya steps and two side shelves hold about 47 LED diyas. Open at the front, no curtain.

Parampara · the journey

The Char Dham wall

India’s four dhams sit at its four corners, too far apart for one map to fit the wall. So the wall shows four glowing pieces of India instead: Uttarakhand, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Odisha. A red pin marks each temple, and a red-and-yellow thread runs to a modern poster about it. Reading right to left, the way visitors walk from the divider, they go clockwise round India: Jagannath Puri (east), Rameswaram (south), Dwarka (west), and Badrinath (north) last before the exit.

Build1 in fire-rated foam, UV printed and contour cut, each piece within a 23 in box on 2 in standoffs with warm LED tape round the back edge. Four 27 × 40 in posters at 2′4″–5′8″. “Char Dham Tirth Yatra” in 12 in gold foam letters runs across the top at 6′7″–7′9″, lit by four picture lights on the wall top.

Notes before you build

  • Walls½ in plywood in 4 × 8 ft modules on 2×4 frames, painted before setup, bolted together and braced with kickers and sandbags, since nothing screws into the gym floor. About 110 ft of outer wall plus the 8½ ft divider and the two Arti returns. Confirm which outer walls the hall or neighbouring sections already give you; each one you share saves its sheets.
  • Foam and fire safetyPlain EPS/XPS foam burns fast. Ask the venue first; most want fire-rated foam board or PVC sheet for the strip, the Char Dham pieces and the foam letters, flame-retardant plywood or FR paint for the walls, and FR fabric for the Annakut and the Arti canopy. All LEDs low-voltage.
  • Lighting37 lights: 34 cordless 16 in picture lights (buy 37) on every board, poster and the Journey wall, and 3 URTOM plug-in spots (buy 2 two-packs) for the entrance poster and rice table. Plus LED tape in the timeline strip, behind the silhouettes and behind the Char Dham pieces, and LED diyas in the alcove. Hall lights off; exit signs stay on. Charge the picture lights overnight; only the spots and LED tape need cords.
  • Arti alcoveThe brief warns against darkened enclosed booths. Keep the front fully open, no curtain; only the top is covered. The diyas are display only, so it doesn’t repeat Jivan Shaili’s interactive diya; confirm with them.
  • AnnakutNo barrier, so the bottom step sits at floor level beside the route. Use sealed or replica food for a multi-day run and keep small children back from it.
  • Ahimsa YagnaNo real flame, heat or smoke. Guard the tile slot so fingers can’t get trapped. Tile and virtue wording needs religious review.
  • CrowdsName and Rice sit under their chapters, so the Riti centre stays open. Places where people stop (tables, the Journey wall, the Puja counter, the Yagna lectern) sit outside the walking line.
  • Reading directionThe route runs counter-clockwise from the SE entry, so visitors walk to their left along every wall and the timeline reads right to left. The card numbers keep the order clear; decide if that is acceptable before printing.
  • ApprovalsPending: Arti handling, the flower offering, name etymologies, Yagna tile pairings, card pronunciations, the Char Dham poster facts and the Char Dham title wording.
  • TimelineOrder foam, prints, LED tape, spots and plywood in the first 3 days, since CNC cutting and printing take about a week. Week 2 is painting, setup and testing. The Media assets tab lists everything to make; give each item an owner this week.

Checked against the lead packet and brief

  • Matches the lead summary: one horizontal life-stage timeline showing all sixteen samskaras, a name-meaning activity, and the names and numbering from packet pp. 3–8 (13 shown as Keshanta · Ritusuddhi).
  • Not placed yet: the crib, book and wedding knot from the lead summary. The open Riti centre has room for a crib near cards 4–5; small ledges under cards 10 and 15 would fit the book and the knot.
  • One difference from the brief: the brief puts the Journey wall on the divider, away from the Riti–Parampara transition. This keeps your sketch’s south-wall position.
  • Sections are named by samskara number, not age, since the brief says samskaras are not fixed-age buckets.
  • Parampara numbering follows walking order (Arti, Thaal, Yagna along the south wall, then Yoga, Puja and the Tirth Yatra wall to the exit), not the packet’s order.
  • Nilkanth Varni’s distance: the packet says “more than 12,000 miles”; the figure usually cited is about 12,000 km (≈ 8,000 miles). Confirm before it goes on a panel.
  • Abhishek is not built here; coordinate with Section 3 as the lead summary says.

Changes since V12

  • The 8 ft entry wall is now a 4 ft freestanding wall straight ahead of the door, 9′-4¾″ in, with 2 ft clear to the south wall. One 48 × 96 in poster covers its whole front so visitors see what the exhibit is about as they walk in (design to come; a placeholder is shown). It replaces the Hindu Riti & Parampara foam letters. The Our Journey board on its back is now 3.9 ft, so Our Journey totals 9.9 ft with the south wall.
  • The Tirth Yatra map and the five tirth posters are gone. In their place, the Char Dham wall: four glowing foam pieces (Uttarakhand, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Odisha), each with a red pin on the temple and a thread to its own 24 × 36 in poster, in order right to left: Jagannath Puri, Rameswaram, Dwarka, Badrinath. The Tirth Yatra (Traveling → Inner discovery) poster is gone too, so the Char Dham wall now runs the whole north wall of Parampara, with 27 × 40 in posters and 23 in pieces set lower on the wall.
  • “Char Dham Tirth Yatra” in 12 in gold foam letters across the top of the north wall at 6′7″–7′9″, like the Shodasha Samskaras title in Riti, lit by four picture lights on the wall top.
  • Lighting: four picture lights over the Char Dham posters and four on the wall top for the title; the two map uplights and the Tirth Yatra poster light are gone, and the map pieces glow from LED tape behind them.
  • The four Char Dham posters in the model now show your final artwork (the 27 × 40 PDFs), in order right to left: Jagannath Puri, Rameswaram, Dwarka, Badrinath.
  • A Structure plan view: walls only, fully dimensioned, with a wall list and a print button, for the build crew.

What changed in V12

  • The entry wall with the Hindu Riti & Parampara sign is now 8 ft long and sits at the middle of the Riti section (15.6 ft from the east wall instead of 5 ft), so the entry lobby is about 9½ × 8 ft.
  • The Our Journey wall wraps the corner: 6.8 ft on the back of the entry wall and 6 ft on the south wall, stopping short of the Arti alcove.
  • “Shodasha Samskaras · Sixteen Sacred Milestones” in gold foam letters above the north-wall boards, with 2½ in clear above and below.
  • Silhouettes are centred on their chapter boards. The visitor route was redrawn to follow the current layout, with a new stop at the Tirth Yatra poster, and the Add your light table now stands just east of the alcove so people pick up a light before stepping in.
  • The stanchion line by the Yoga wall has a fourth post (11¾ ft).
  • The Puja, Thaal, Yoga, Tirth Yatra and Ahimsa Yagna posters and all six chapter boards use the latest artwork. The Tirth Yatra poster (31 × 60 in) replaces Pilgrim or tourist? beside the divider.
  • Lighting is now your two products: 33 battery picture lights over every board, poster and the Journey wall, and 5 URTOM plug-in spots for the entry sign, the map and the rice table. Numbers are in the Lighting tab.
  • The growing footprints are gone.
  • The whole timeline is lower: strip 3′–3′10″, chapter boards 4′–6′8″. Silhouettes are scaled to 78% (tallest 30 in), lift flaps and mirrors sit under the strip, and the First Letters table is 2′6″ with a small tabletop guide (about 3 ft overall).
  • A second stanchion line runs west from the end of the Marriage/Farewell divider, so people coming past the Arti alcove carry on to the Thaal, Yagna and Yoga before turning to Puja.
  • Spot lights follow the new heights and positions: 40 in all (16 tile spots plus 24 for the stations, posters and the Journey corner).
  • The Arti alcove moved right to the Marriage/Farewell divider (then 1 ft back left, below). The Add your light table now stands on its west side.
  • The 8 ft exit wall in Parampara is gone, so the whole north wall reads as one Tirth Yatra wall. Three belt stanchions stand on its line to keep visitors on the route.
  • Entry and exit openings are both the standard 4 ft.
  • The Thaal and Ahimsa Yagna posters (and the kund) moved 1 ft right; the Arti alcove moved 1 ft back left, so it now spans 17.8–22.6 ft.
  • Silhouettes, chapter boards, samskara tiles and the Arti, Puja, Thaal, Yoga and Pilgrim posters now use the final artwork and cut files.
